title: 50,000 Buddhas Carved Into One Chinese Hillside — Dazu | China Travel Expert
description:
More than 50,000 Buddhas were carved by hand into these cliffs — and it took over 250 years to finish.

The Dazu Rock Carvings in Chongqing spread across 141 sites and hold over 50,000 statues. The earliest were begun around 650 AD in the Tang dynasty, and the work reached its peak under the Song. What makes Dazu rare is that Buddhism, Taoism and Confucianism share the same cliffs, side by side — a stone record of three faiths living together. At Baodingshan a reclining Nirvana Buddha stretches more than 30 metres, and 800-year-old paint still clings to the rock. UNESCO listed it in 1999 as "a masterpiece of human creative genius."

🧭 Expert Tip: Start at Baodingshan (Treasured Summit) for the grandest, best-preserved tableaux — then loop to Beishan for the older, smaller niches; give yourself a half day for both.
